kaziranga.overview: Northeast India's walking runs through dense forests and rolling hills. The standout day hike descends thousands of steep stone steps to the living root bridges of Nongriat in Meghalaya. Further afield, the Dzukou Valley in Nagaland provides a lush, rolling trek, though visitors must secure the required permits for Nagaland and Arunachal Pradesh before setting out.

months.4: Heat and humidity build as early showers begin, making the long climbs out of the valleys slow and tiring.
months.12: Dry, cool air and clear days suit the long stone-step descents to Nongriat and the ridgelines of the Dzukou Valley.

kerala.overview: Kerala's best walking lies inland in the Western Ghats, where trails wind through tea estates, shola forests, and high-altitude grasslands. The main route is the long day hike up Meesapulimala near Munnar, which requires an advance permit and an authorized guide. The dry months offer the clearest views of the rolling green peaks, while the heavy summer monsoon brings leeches and washes out trails.

months.2: Rain and swell persist, so boat days can be rough. The short trails on Padar and Rinca stay muddy and slippery.
months.5: The dry season is well established, with firm paths on Padar and calmer seas for the boat trips between islands.
months.6: Clear skies and calm seas make the steep sunrise climb on Padar a reliable plan, with cooler early mornings.
months.7: Dry, steady weather keeps the dirt path up Padar firm. Mornings are the best time to climb, before the heat builds.
months.8: The driest weeks bring hard-baked, dusty trails on Padar and on the flat ranger-guided walks across Komodo and Rinca.
months.9: Dry heat builds across the scrub, so walks on Komodo and Rinca are best at dawn. The Padar climb is firm and clear.
months.10: Heat increases and the first clouds appear, but the island trails are still dry and the boat crossings mostly calm.

months.1: Summer heat is intense, and the multi-day wilderness trails do not run. Short guided bush walks go out at first light, before the day warms up.
months.2: Heat and humidity stay high, and the wilderness trails are closed for the season. Guided walks stay short and start at dawn.
months.5: Dry, cool mornings and thinning vegetation make May a good time to start. The three-night wilderness trails and daily bush walks run reliably.
months.6: Cool, dry days and thinner bush make wildlife easier to spot from the trail. Wilderness trails and daily guided walks both run.
months.7: July brings crisp mornings and the clearest sightlines of the year, so guided walks cover ground comfortably in cool air.
months.8: Dry weather and open bush continue. The multi-day trails run reliably, and water holes draw wildlife as the land dries.
months.11: Heat builds again and the wilderness trails are closed. Early-morning guided walks remain the main way to go on foot.
months.12: Hot, humid days keep the wilderness trails closed. Short guided walks at dawn are still available, with green summer bush closing in the views.

kyrgyzstan.overview: Kyrgyzstan's trekking runs through the Tian Shan mountains, where routes cross steep passes to reach glacier-fed lakes and summer pastures. The signature multi-day routes, like the three-to-four-day Ala-Kul trek or hikes between yurt camps at Song-Köl, deliver big alpine scenery. Most trails start from remote dirt road trailheads, and routes near the borders require advance permits.

months.1: Deep snow and bitter cold close the high treks and yurt camps. Walking is limited to short snowy paths in the lowest valleys.
months.2: Snow cover is at its deepest and the high treks stay closed. Only short valley walks near the towns are practical.
months.3: The snow begins to soften at low elevations, but the high passes and yurt camps remain closed.
months.7: The prime trekking window opens in full, with the high passes mostly clear of snow and the alpine lakes reachable.
months.8: High pastures are dotted with grazing flocks and yurt camps, and the Ala-Kul and Song-Köl routes are at their most reliable.
months.11: Deep winter sets in, and the high routes are impassable. Short walks in the lowest valleys are all that remain.
months.12: The mountains are locked in deep snow. Only snowshoeing or short walks in the lowest valleys are possible.

ladakh.overview: Ladakh is a high-altitude desert of stark, jagged peaks and deep valleys, offering dramatic Himalayan trekking. The classic route is the Markha Valley trek, a multi-day journey crossing passes over 16,000 feet past remote villages and Buddhist monasteries. Day hikers can tackle steep acclimatization trails around Leh or explore the Sham Valley. The season is short, dictated by snow on the high passes, with the best walking from June to September.

months.1: Deep winter snow closes the high passes and trekking routes, and the region is largely cut off by road.
months.2: The mountains remain locked in snow and the trails are impassable.
months.3: Snow still blankets the high country and the passes stay closed.
months.12: The region is snowbound and cut off by road, and the trails are impassable.

lake-district.overview: The Lake District is defined by steep, rugged fells and deep glacial valleys holding ribbon lakes. Walkers tackle steep ascents up Scafell Pike and Helvellyn, where high ridges like Striding Edge require a head for heights and offer sweeping panoramas over the Cumbrian landscape. Lower elevations provide miles of graded paths around lakes like Derwentwater and Windermere. Multi-day walkers can cross the park on the 70-mile Cumbria Way.

months.6: Peak hiking weather brings long, mild days perfect for long link-ups of multiple summits. The trails are dry and the high ridges are fully accessible.

lapland.overview: Finnish Lapland offers vast forests and rolling fells for walkers seeking remote wilderness. The region is famous for multi-day hut-to-hut routes like the 34-mile Hetta-Pallas trail and the 50-mile Karhunkierros trek, alongside shorter day hikes to open summits. The walking season is short, peaking in early autumn when the fells turn red and gold.

months.2: Snow lies deep and the cold is fierce. Snowshoeing on groomed winter trails is the way to explore, as the summer routes lie buried.
months.6: Summer brings near-constant daylight and the trails dry out enough for the long treks. Heavy mosquitoes emerge in the forests, making insect repellent essential.
months.7: Near-endless daylight allows hiking at any hour. The multi-day routes are fully accessible, though mosquitoes remain intense in the lower forests.
months.9: This is the peak month for walking, driven by the ruska autumn colors that turn the fells red and gold. The air is crisp and the mosquitoes are largely gone.
months.11: Daylight fades fast and the first deep snow settles. Walkers use snowshoes or stay on short, groomed paths around the villages.
months.12: Snow piles up in near-continuous darkness. Walkers stay on snowshoe tracks and short groomed paths around the villages.

lisbon.overview: Hiking around Lisbon means escaping the city for the forested hills of Sintra or the coastal ridges of Arrábida Natural Park. Trails range from easy paths between Sintra's palaces to day hikes along the Serra do Risco, offering views over the Atlantic Ocean. The best walking happens in the mild spring and fall, avoiding the summer heat.

months.3: Spring arrives with blooming wildflowers along the Serra do Risco and comfortable temperatures for day hikes.
months.12: Winter walking is mild though often wet, along the paths through the Sintra forests.

lofoten.overview: The Lofoten Islands offer dramatic coastal hiking, with trails climbing steep granite ridges that drop directly into the Norwegian Sea. Walkers come for steep day hikes that earn wide fjord and ocean panoramas, often under the midnight sun. The signature routes are short but relentlessly steep, like the stone staircase up Reinebringen or the rugged descent to the isolated sands of Kvalvika Beach. The best conditions run from late June through August.

months.1: Deep snow, ice and the polar night shut down the mountain trails. Walking is limited to short, flat coastal paths near the villages, with microspikes or snowshoes needed.
months.2: Deep snow and ice keep the peaks closed to walkers as daylight slowly returns. Only short, flat coastal paths near the villages are practical, with microspikes or snowshoes.
months.7: The peak hiking window brings near-constant daylight and mostly snow-free trails, the best time for steep ascents like Reinebringen.
months.8: Trails are dry and snow-free and the evenings begin to darken, so ridge views come in gentler light. Showers become more frequent.
months.12: The polar night and deep snow close the mountain trails. Short, flat coastal paths near the villages are all that remain, and they need microspikes or snowshoes.

months.5: Late spring is a good time to walk. The woodlands are lush, and the trails along the North Downs are generally dry.
months.7: Warm temperatures make for pleasant walking on the shaded paths of Epping Forest or the breezy ridges of the North Downs.
months.8: Late summer remains good for day hikes. The trails are dry, and the views from Box Hill stretch clearly across the landscape.
months.9: Early autumn offers crisp air and comfortable temperatures for a long walk along the river or through the woodlands.
months.10: Autumn colors peak in Epping Forest. Trails begin to soften with seasonal rain, but the walking remains rewarding.
